module_title: Railway Zones, Headquarters, and Mountain Railways
introduction: To efficiently manage and operate such a colossal network, Indian Railways is divided into geographically designated 'Zones', which are further sub-divided into 'Divisions'. At this level, we will map out the major zones and their headquarters, while also studying the engineering marvels and UNESCO-recognized mountain railways.

core_concepts.title: Railway Zones and Headquarters
core_concepts.description: Currently, India is divided into '18 Railway Zones' (including the Kolkata Metro). The headquarters of the primary cardinal directions are: 1. Northern Railway - New Delhi. 2. Southern Railway - Chennai. 3. Eastern Railway - Kolkata. 4. Western Railway - Churchgate, Mumbai. 5. Central Railway - CSMT, Mumbai.

core_concepts.title: The Newest Zone
core_concepts.description: The 18th and newest railway zone in India is the 'South Coast Railway' (SCoR). It was announced recently, and its operational headquarters is located in the port city of 'Visakhapatnam' (Andhra Pradesh).

core_concepts.title: Konkan Railway
core_concepts.description: This is a modern engineering marvel of Indian Railways that connects 'Roha' (in Maharashtra) to 'Mangaluru' (in Karnataka) along the western coast. Spanning 760 km, it passes through the extremely rugged and mountainous terrain of the Western Ghats, featuring over 2,000 bridges and 91 tunnels. It significantly reduced the travel time between Mumbai and southern India.

core_concepts.title: Mountain Railways of India
core_concepts.description: These are historic narrow-gauge lines built during the British era to connect the plains to high-altitude hill stations. Three of these mountain railways have been collectively designated as a 'UNESCO World Heritage Site': 1. Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (West Bengal), 2. Nilgiri Mountain Railway (Tamil Nadu), and 3. Kalka-Shimla Railway (Himachal Pradesh).

important_entities.name: Kolkata
important_entities.significance: Kolkata holds a unique position in the railway network. It is the only city in India that serves as the headquarters for 3 distinct railway zones: The Eastern Railway, the South Eastern Railway, and the Kolkata Metro.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often logically guess that 'North Central' or 'South Central' HQs would be near Delhi or Chennai. Do not fall for this. The North Central Railway HQ is in 'Prayagraj' (Allahabad), and the South Central Railway HQ is in 'Secunderabad'. Memorize these exceptions separately.

Exams frequently ask which states the Konkan Railway passes through. Remember: It runs through Maharashtra, Goa, and Karnataka. It 'does NOT enter Kerala' (it terminates at Mangaluru, just north of the Kerala border).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The four historic metropolitan cities directly correspond to the four cardinal direction railway headquarters.

exam_strategy_tips: 'Match the following' questions regarding headquarters are virtually guaranteed. Specifically focus on memorizing Hajipur (East Central), Jabalpur (West Central), and Gorakhpur (North Eastern).
Rote memorize the names of the 3 UNESCO Mountain Railways. Examiners often throw in 'Matheran Light Railway' or 'Kangra Valley' as trap options (these do NOT have UNESCO status).
